domain: Islamic Jurisprudence / Quranic Hermeneutics / Legal Theory
topic_summary: Analysis of the Islamic principle of naskh (abrogation) in Quranic interpretation. The fixed substrate is the Quranic text itself and the methodological principle of naskh. Two primary readings contest how to resolve apparent textual contradictions: Classical Abrogation (later verses supersede earlier ones based on chronology) versus Contextual Harmonization (all verses remain valid within their contexts).

key_entities: Quranic text (fixed revealed scripture, approximately 114 surahs over 23 years)
Classical abrogation school (Shafi'i, Hanbali majority position)
Contextual harmonization school (modernist, some Hanafi interpretations)
Legal jurists (mujtahidun - those authorized to derive law)
Ordinary believers (muqallidun - those who follow established rulings)
State legal systems (where Sharia is codified or referenced)
key_tensions: Textual contradiction resolution: chronological supersession vs contextual preservation
Hermeneutic authority: jurist consensus based on abrogation vs interpretive pluralism
key_mechanisms: Naskh mechanism: Later revelation invalidates earlier ruling on same topic (Classical reading)
Contextual specification: Each verse applies to its situational context (Harmonization reading)
key_absences: Absence of definitive chronological ordering for all Quranic verses (only partial scholarly consensus)
Absence of explicit meta-textual abrogation markers within the Quran itself
Absence of discussion on who adjudicates which reading is authoritative in pluralistic contexts

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The Quranic text as fixed divine revelation combined with the methodological principle of naskh (abrogation) for resolving apparent textual contradictions
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Interpretive legitimacy grounded in scholarly consensus (ijma) within madhabs (legal schools), with classical schools deriving authority from chronological revelation order and harmonization schools deriving authority from divine unity and contextual coherence

readings.commitment: Later Quranic verses abrogate earlier verses on the same legal/theological topic based on chronological revelation order
readings.authority_grounding: Scholarly consensus (ijma) within classical madhabs; chronological ordering of revelation as determinative
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fixed legal rulings with clear supersession hierarchy; abrogated verses lose legal force but retain spiritual/historical value; benefits legal certainty, victims are interpretive flexibility and theological coherence when verses appear contradictory

readings.commitment: All Quranic verses remain valid within their specific revelatory and situational contexts; apparent contradictions resolved through contextual specification rather than chronological supersession
readings.authority_grounding: Divine unity (tawhid) and Quranic completeness; modernist and some classical Hanafi interpretive traditions
readings.expected_structural_delta: Flexible legal interpretation requiring contextual analysis; all verses retain legal potential depending on circumstance; benefits theological coherence and adaptability, victims are legal predictability and jurist authority to definitively close questions

readings.commitment: Quranic revelation progressively restricted permissions rather than abrogating earlier rulings; movement from permissive to restrictive represents divine pedagogy not textual invalidation
readings.authority_grounding: Pedagogical reading of revelation as gradual reform; historical sequence as teaching method rather than legal hierarchy
readings.expected_structural_delta: Earlier permissive verses understood as transitional accommodations not permanent law; later restrictions represent final divine intent; benefits evolutionary legal reading, victims are those who cite earlier permissive texts for contemporary practice

axiom_contradictions.basis: Classical abrogation's foundational axiom that later revelation invalidates earlier text cannot coexist with contextual harmonization's axiom that all revelation remains valid in context. Accepting one requires rejecting the other as a coherent hermeneutic principle, though both can socially coexist as competing schools.

Classical abrogation treats supersession as binary (verse X no longer applies) while progressive restriction treats it as pedagogical layering (verse X was always provisional). A single framework cannot hold both that a verse is genuinely abrogated and that it was pedagogically transitional without collapsing into one or the other.

omegas.description: Classical abrogation depends on precise chronological ordering of revelation. Scholarly consensus exists for some verse clusters but not all. What is the epistemological status of abrogation claims when chronology is contested? Does uncertainty collapse the reading or shift it from Mountain to Rope of scholarly convention?

In pluralistic contexts where multiple readings coexist (e.g., diaspora communities, secular states with Muslim populations), who adjudicates which reading is authoritative for legal purposes? Is this a Snare where state power resolves hermeneutic contest, or a Scaffold of emerging transnational interpretive networks?

Classical scholars disagree on the number of abrogated verses (estimates range from 5 to over 500). Does this divergence indicate the reading itself is unstable, or does it reflect different thresholds for what counts as abrogation? Potential reclassification from Tangled Rope to Rope of scholarly convention.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (operational medium of classical jurisprudence) + extraction absence
